questions_used.question: Q1 — which C4 levels, and which box is the zoom parent?
questions_used.answer: L1 system context with the manager as one box marked as the zoom parent; L2 containers enclosed in a dotted box; L3 only if the source states container internals (it does not); L4 out of scope.

questions_used.question: Q2 — one L2 diagram or two?
questions_used.answer: Measured on the frozen build: one L2 diagram does not exist at the mandated direction. 17 containers / 23 relations in one diagram at `lr` exits 1 ('no obstacle-safe route for wapi -> q; increase node/layer spacing': probe-budget-lr), and the same section in `tb` is refused by the build itself ('17 nodes / 23 edges, above the readable budget (12/16)', 105x171, 23 crossings, 73 near-miss cells, 1 skipped label: probe-budget-tb). So L2 ships as two enclosed halves whose union covers all 23 relations, and both are `enclosed` so the reader sees one dotted world per half.
questions_used.answer_source: own judgment — reason: measured engine behaviour on 2b1dd353 (recorded probes, attempts-log.jsonl)

questions_used.question: Q3 — reading direction?
questions_used.answer: All diagrams left-to-right: the canvas declares `direction: "lr"` once and no diagram overrides it (check reports direction=lr).
questions_used.answer_source: brief framing (owner directive: keep one direction across diagrams)

questions_used.question: Q4 — does the dotted box wrap the external systems too?
questions_used.answer: Yes: a C4 container diagram shows the containers together with the external systems they exchange data with, and the enclosure rule is that no route may cross the dotted line. Putting S3, Slack, providers and machines inside the box keeps every relation inside it, so enclosure-crossings stay 0; the boundary of the box is the system boundary, and the external boxes inside are drawn in the external hue family.
questions_used.answer_source: own judgment — reason: C4 container-view convention plus the engine's 'routes never cross the dotted line' rule; both satisfied by one box around all contents

questions_used.question: Q5 — motion?
questions_used.answer: One dot per live transition only, none on state writes or on the enclosure border: 11 single-dot routes (http, provider API, boot request/response, allocate, and the agent's heartbeat + Slack alert).
questions_used.answer_source: brief framing + source.md ('slow, sparse dots on selected communication edges; never on borders', 'keep on dot alive per line')

questions_used.question: Q6 — which qualifiers must be on the canvas?
questions_used.answer: Every qualifier the source states, spelled on the canvas: 'create/terminate/repair', 'reinstall/reprovision', 'verify reimage', 'boot.ipxe + S3 args', 'gcore sync, 1 min', 'run machine-audit', 'register + heartbeat', 'diagnostic events', 'proposed actions', 'confirm + alerts', 'diagnose uploads', 'pull boot image', 'allocate instance'. No qualifier is left to the ledger this round.
questions_used.answer_source: brief framing (owner directive: 'verify reimage' and 'args' were judged missing)

questions_used.question: Q7 — is a two-part L2 still one C4 level?
questions_used.answer: Yes: both halves are the container level of the same system, each holds a subset of the same 17 containers and they share the group hue families, so a reader sees level 2 twice rather than two levels. Each description says it is inside the dotted box.
questions_used.answer_source: own judgment — reason: the engine cannot hold the level in one section (measured), and dropping relations to fit would fail coverage

questions_used.question: Q8 — is a folded context direction a dropped relation?
questions_used.answer: No: the context box folds the manager→machines lifecycle into one aggregate ('boot + audit + heartbeat'); both boot directions and the heartbeat are drawn verbatim at L2 (l2a:e7 iPXE request, l2a:e8 boot.ipxe + S3 args, l2b:e3 register + heartbeat), and the expansion is recorded in the coverage map. Nothing from the 23 relations is missing anywhere on the canvas.
questions_used.answer_source: own judgment — reason: C4 context is an interaction-per-external-system zoom; the brief's rule is that a context edge expands into container edges rather than repeating or dropping them

triage.converged_when: Levels, zoom parent, direction, enclosure scope, motion and the on-canvas qualifier list were all fixed by the brief; the only open question was whether L2 fits one section, and that was answered by measurement rather than a question.

classification.evidence: the source's own path list fans out of one queue/machine spine (q -> reg, ssh, s3, jan, db; mch -> boot, s3, agent) with one live dot per line — the lifecycle-machine signature carried over from round 13.
tie_breakers_considered: Density: 23 relations over 17 containers; not a chain, not a dense fabric.
Anti-parallel pair (machines <-> boot server) — borrows the service-mesh habit of keeping both directions in one diagram; they ship together in l2a.
Identifier/qualifier content is now heavy on the canvas (protocols, payloads, periodicities) but the layout is still fan-shaped, so the family stays lifecycle-machines.
classification.secondary_recipe: service-meshes: the anti-parallel boot pair in ONE enclosed diagram with distinct labels and ports; the queue's fan declared in the source's listing order.

view_shape.rung_chosen: rung 2 — ONE pannable canvas with three described diagrams (zoom chain, not a repetition of the same box)
source_facts_that_decided_it: The brief asks for a zoom chain: the parent box in L1, the expanded contents in L2.
The container level cannot be one section at the mandated direction (measured twice on the frozen build).
The canvas form is what carries per-diagram titles/descriptions, and the engine's new uniform dividers + top rule make the bands read evenly.
